findings.section: §7 Implementation Assessment — Monitoring baseline / MVP phases Phase 1
findings.title: synchronous_commit config-knob declaration still incomplete after fixer pass
findings.detail: The iteration-1 finding OP-ADR-01-003 (C5) asked for a full runtime-config declaration: parameter name, expected value(s), default, and configuration location. The fixer pass added a monitoring hook ('Config drift — alert if synchronous_commit deviates') which surfaces the parameter name but does not supply the expected value (e.g., on or remote_write), the default value, or the configuration location (e.g., postgresql.conf, or the managed-service parameter group path). C5 requires the full knob tuple so an operator can confirm the parameter is set correctly post-provisioning without consulting external documentation. The Phase 1 risk row still notes 'Synchronous mode silently degrades to async (breaks RPO=0)' — the monitoring hook catches drift after the fact, but no authoritative expected value is declared to anchor the alert threshold.
findings.recommendation: Expand the monitoring baseline entry for synchronous_commit to a C5 config-knob declaration inline: parameter name (synchronous_commit), expected value (on), default (off in many managed tiers — note the divergence), and configuration location (postgresql.conf or managed-service parameter group, as appropriate for the chosen platform). This lets an operator verify correctness at provisioning time, and anchors the config-drift alert to a named expected value rather than an implicit one.
